annotations.annotation_text: Oneiric dimension "sleep" on page 578 ("The Bedroom Scene"): the nocturnal consciousness surfaces within HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. During this Age of Men (closing) phase, Joyce reconstructs the sleeping body's sensory deprivation — dimmed sight, distorted hearing, dream-logic association — transforming somatic experience into polyphonic language.

annotations.annotation_text: Liturgical echo "Amen" on page 578 ("The Bedroom Scene"): Catholic ritual, Latin prayer, and sacramental language weave through HCE and ALP in bed, the children's cries, attempted sexual intercourse, domestic reality intruding on the cosmic dream. Joyce fuses ecclesiastical solemnity with domestic banality during the Age of Men (closing) phase, treating the tavern counter as communion rail and the sleeping body as sacred vessel.
